author: swain
title: Gate public person-profile reads behind a service-read M2M tier
body:
`GET /v1/public-person-profiles`, `/published` and `/unlisted` were `@PublicAccess` with no auth. `/unlisted` returns every personId with an active privacy removal or a deleted profile, so anyone could pull the list of people who asked us to take their page down. The render gate leaks the same fact one person at a time through its `{ removed: true }` marker.

The only real consumer is gp-marketing, server-side, and it already holds a Clerk M2M JWT for its machine. So these three reads now require a credential: that JWT, a full `mt_` M2M token, an admin, or (render gate only) the logged-in owner of the requested personId. The owner clause keeps the release-train e2e in `public-profile-editor.spec.ts` working, since it reads its own minted personId as a plain user. Voter-density and claim-request stay open.

Why a separate tier instead of reusing `m2mToken`: `@clerk/backend`'s `m2m.verify` checks a JWT-format M2M token against the instance JWKS and exp/nbf only. It does not check scopes or our machine secret, so any machine in our Clerk instance can mint a JWT that verifies. If that set `request.m2mToken`, every `AdminOrM2MGuard`/`M2MOnly`/`UserOrM2M` route would open to any machine. Instead a verified JWT sets `request.serviceReader`, which only `ServiceReadGuard` honours, and it gets past `SessionGuard` only on `@PublicAccess` routes (401 elsewhere). Opaque `mt_` tokens are verified server-side against `GP_API_MACHINE_SECRET` and keep full M2M exactly as before.

**Merge order: do not merge this until the companion gp-marketing PR (which sends the JWT as `Authorization: Bearer` on these reads) is live in gp-marketing prod (`master`).** Merging to `main` auto-deploys gp-api to prod, and an unauthenticated gp-marketing would then get 403s on the render gate and the sitemap feeds.

Known dev-only degradation: gp-marketing preview and develop deployments mint their token from the prod Clerk instance, so gp-api-dev will reject it once this reaches dev. Those environments will see 403s on these reads until they get a dev-instance token.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Authentication and privacy-sensitive API behavior change with a hard dependency on gp-marketing deploying first; mis-ordering causes 403s in prod, and JWT M2M is intentionally weaker than opaque M2M so guard wiring must stay correct.
> 
> **Overview**
> Closes a privacy gap on three **public person-profile reads** (`GET /v1/public-person-profiles`, `/published`, `/unlisted`) that previously had no credential check while exposing privacy-takedown signals. Those routes now use **`ServiceReadGuard`**, which admits a Clerk **JWT-format M2M** token (`mch_*` → `request.serviceReader`), full opaque **`mt_*` M2M**, admins, or (render gate only) the logged-in **owner** of the queried `personId`. Voter-density and claim-request stay browser-open on the same `@PublicAccess` controller.
> 
> **`SessionGuard`** and **`ClerkAuthService`** split machine auth into two tiers: opaque `mt_*` still sets **`request.m2mToken`** (full M2M for existing guards); JWT M2M is verified via JWKS only, sets **`serviceReader`** (never `m2mToken`), and only clears the global guard on `@PublicAccess` routes—so JWT M2M cannot reach `AdminOrM2MGuard` / normal session routes. ADR and agent docs describe the model; tests and `signTestM2MJwt` cover the new path.
> 
> **Deploy note:** gp-marketing must send the JWT on these reads before gp-api prod ships this change.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 4bcac394cac65f994be6d6c4d30b7210c70a657d. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

 - Caller services don't manage their own keys; rotation goes through Clerk.
 - people-api used a separate model (S2S JWT) because it predated this decision. That is moot now: gp-api reads voter data from Databricks and the S2S path is gone, so Clerk M2M is the only machine-auth model left.
 - Public routes still need `@PublicAccess()`; the guard chain runs even when no token is present.
+
+## Update: JWT-format M2M tokens are a read tier
+
+Clerk can also issue M2M tokens as JWTs (`sub` starts with `mch_`). `@clerk/backend` verifies those against the instance JWKS and `exp`/`nbf` only; it does not check scopes or the machine secret, so any machine in the Clerk instance can mint one that verifies. `SessionGuard` therefore tags a verified JWT M2M token as `request.serviceReader`, never `request.m2mToken`, and honours it only on `@PublicAccess()` routes. `ServiceReadGuard` admits it (along with full M2M, admins, and the owner of the requested `personId`) on the public person-profile reads that gp-marketing calls server-side. Opaque `mt_*` tokens keep full M2M as before.

@@ -26,6 +27,16 @@ Auth state is enforced globally via three guards registered in order. Most route
 ## Patterns
 
 - **Global guards run in order**: `SessionGuard` → `RolesGuard` (`SessionGuard` wired as `APP_GUARD` in `app.module.ts`, `RolesGuard` in `authentication.module.ts`). M2M `mt_*` tokens are verified inside `SessionGuard`. New guards belong route-level, not global, unless they're truly cross-cutting.
+- **Clerk M2M has two tiers.** An opaque `mt_*` token is verified by Clerk
+  against `GP_API_MACHINE_SECRET`, which enforces machine scope, and sets
+  `request.m2mToken` — full M2M, trusted by `AdminOrM2MGuard`, `M2MOnly` and
+  `UserOrM2M`. A JWT-format M2M token (`sub` starts with `mch_`) is verified
+  only against the instance JWKS; Clerk checks neither its scopes nor our
+  secret, so any machine in the instance can mint one. It sets
+  `request.serviceReader`, never `m2mToken`, and passes `SessionGuard` only on
+  `@PublicAccess()` routes (401 elsewhere). Gate a read for it with
+  `ServiceReadGuard`. gp-marketing reads the public person-profile endpoints
+  this way.
 - **`@PublicAccess()` is the only escape hatch.** Don't conditionally skip auth inside a guard — opt out at the route level.
 - **Absence of `@Roles()` = "any authenticated user".** `routeIsPublicAndNoRoles.util.ts` is what makes that work; don't rely on the decorator being present to imply auth.
 - Password resets issue a **short-lived JWT**, not a DB-stored token. Side effects after consumption must be done in the same request.

@@ -0,0 +1,156 @@
+import axios from 'axios'
+import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken'
+import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
+import { UserRole } from '../../generated/prisma'
+import {
+  AUTH_PROVIDER_TOKEN,
+  AuthProvider,
+} from '@/authentication/interfaces/auth-provider.interface'
+import { signTestM2MJwt, useTestService } from '@/test-service'
+
+const service = useTestService()
+
+const PERSON_ID = '33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333'
+
+const READS = [
+  { path: '/v1/public-person-profiles', params: { personId: PERSON_ID } },
+  { path: '/v1/public-person-profiles/published', params: {} },
+  { path: '/v1/public-person-profiles/unlisted', params: {} },
+]
+
+const withBearer = (token: string) => ({
+  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
+})
+
+describe('ServiceReadGuard on the public person-profile reads', () => {
+  it.each(READS)('403s $path with no token', async ({ path, params }) => {
+    const res = await axios.get(path, {
+      baseURL: service.client.defaults.baseURL,
+      params,
+      validateStatus: () => true,
+    })
+    expect(res.status).toBe(403)
+  })
+
+  it.each(READS)(
+    '403s $path for a logged-in user who is not the owner',
+    async ({ path, params }) => {
+      const res = await service.client.get(path, { params })
+      expect(res.status).toBe(403)
+    },
+  )
+
+  it.each(READS)(
+    'serves $path to a JWT-format M2M token',
+    async ({ path, params }) => {
+      await service.prisma.personProfileRemoval.create({
+        data: { personId: PERSON_ID, appliedBy: 'ops@goodparty.org' },
+      })
+      const res = await service.client.get(path, {
+        params,
+        ...withBearer(signTestM2MJwt()),
+      })
+      expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+    },
+  )
+
+  it.each(READS)(
+    'serves $path to an opaque mt_ M2M token',
+    async ({ path, params }) => {
+      vi.spyOn(
+        service.app.get<AuthProvider>(AUTH_PROVIDER_TOKEN),
+        'verifyM2MToken',
+      ).mockResolvedValue({ id: 'mt_test', subject: 'test-machine' })
+      await service.prisma.personProfileRemoval.create({
+        data: { personId: PERSON_ID, appliedBy: 'ops@goodparty.org' },
+      })
+      const res = await service.client.get(path, {
+        params,
+        ...withBearer('mt_test'),
+      })
+      expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+    },
+  )
+
+  it.each(READS)('serves $path to an admin', async ({ path, params }) => {
+    await service.prisma.user.update({
+      where: { id: service.user.id },
+      data: { roles: [UserRole.admin] },
+    })
+    await service.prisma.personProfileRemoval.create({
+      data: { personId: PERSON_ID, appliedBy: 'ops@goodparty.org' },
+    })
+    const res = await service.client.get(path, { params })
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+  })
+
+  it('403s a JWT signed with the wrong key, even with an mch_ subject', async () => {
+    const forged = jwt.sign({ sub: 'mch_forged' }, 'not-the-secret', {
+      expiresIn: '1h',
+    })
+    const res = await service.client.get(
+      '/v1/public-person-profiles/unlisted',
+      {
+        ...withBearer(forged),
+      },
+    )
+    expect(res.status).toBe(403)
+  })
+
+  it('serves the render gate to the owner of the requested personId', async () => {
+    // The release-train e2e reads its own minted personId as a plain user.
+    await service.prisma.user.update({
+      where: { id: service.user.id },
+      data: { personId: PERSON_ID },
+    })
+    await service.prisma.personProfileRemoval.create({
+      data: { personId: PERSON_ID, appliedBy: 'ops@goodparty.org' },
+    })
+
+    const res = await service.client.get('/v1/public-person-profiles', {
+      params: { personId: PERSON_ID.toUpperCase() },
+    })
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+    expect(res.data.removed).toBe(true)
+  })
+
+  it("403s the render gate for someone else's personId", async () => {
+    await service.prisma.user.update({
+      where: { id: service.user.id },
+      data: { personId: '44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444' },
+    })
+
+    const res = await service.client.get('/v1/public-person-profiles', {
+      params: { personId: PERSON_ID },
+    })
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(403)
+  })
+
+  it('does not let a JWT-format M2M token through AdminOrM2MGuard', async () => {
+    // Any machine in the Clerk instance can mint a JWT that verifies, so it
+    // must stay a read tier and never act as a full M2M caller.
+    const res = await service.client.post(
+      '/v1/person-profiles/removals',
+      { personId: PERSON_ID, appliedBy: 'privacy@goodparty.org' },
+      withBearer(signTestM2MJwt()),
+    )
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(401)
+    expect(
+      await service.prisma.personProfileRemoval.count({
+        where: { personId: PERSON_ID },
+      }),
+    ).toBe(0)
+  })
+
+  it('does not let a JWT-format M2M token onto a plain authenticated route', async () => {
+    const res = await service.client.get(
+      '/v1/person-profiles/mine',
+      withBearer(signTestM2MJwt()),
+    )
+
+    expect(res.status).toBe(401)
+  })
+})

@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@
+import { CanActivate, ExecutionContext, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'
+import { UserRole } from '../../generated/prisma'
+import { IncomingRequest } from '@/authentication/authentication.types'
+import { effectiveUser } from '@/authentication/util/effectiveUser.util'
+
+@Injectable()
+export class ServiceReadGuard implements CanActivate {
+  canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean {
+    const req = context
+      .switchToHttp()
+      .getRequest<IncomingRequest & { query?: Record<string, unknown> }>()
+    if (req.serviceReader || req.m2mToken) {
+      return true
+    }
+    if (effectiveUser(req)?.roles.includes(UserRole.admin)) {
+      return true
+    }
+    const ownPersonId = req.user?.personId
+    const requestedPersonId = req.query?.personId
+    return (
+      typeof ownPersonId === 'string' &&
+      typeof requestedPersonId === 'string' &&
+      ownPersonId.toLowerCase() === requestedPersonId.toLowerCase()
+    )
+  }
+}
